# Create E4 Phaser gym scene

## Problem statement

Create a Phaser gym scene demonstrating the E4 Phaser enemy — the orbital pattern attacker from GDD §4.1. The scene should show its circular neon ring appearance with a central core, slow orbital path movement, and predictable repeating firing cycles. This is a Level 5 exclusive enemy with high pattern-based challenge.

## Users

- **Player / developer** testing enemy behaviour — wants to see the Phaser's orbital movement and predictable firing patterns in isolation.
- **AI agents implementing AI_Hell** — need a reference implementation of orbital movement and pattern-based firing logic.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want to see Phaser enemies move in fixed orbital paths around a central point so I can verify the orbital movement code works correctly.
- As a **developer**, I want to click a button to destroy a random Phaser and see its explosion animation so I can verify destruction logic.
- As a **developer**, I want to toggle the Phaser's shooting behaviour on/off so I can test both orbital-only and shooting modes independently.
- As a **developer**, I want to see clear tell animations and advance audio cues (≥ 500 ms lead time) before the Phaser fires so I can verify the telegraphing system.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Gym scene exists:** A Phaser scene (`src/scenes/gym/GymPhaser.ts`) renders Phaser enemies in orbital paths around a central point.
- [ ] **AC2 — Phaser visual style:** Phasers render as circular neon rings with a central core (magenta `#ff00ff` per GDD §4.1) consistent with the player ship aesthetic.
- [ ] **AC3 — Orbital movement:** Enemies move slowly in fixed orbital paths around a central point on screen.
- [ ] **AC4 — Predictable firing patterns:** When shoot mode is toggled on, Phasers fire in predictable, repeating cycles (radial or aimed patterns) with clear tell animations and advance audio cues (≥ 500 ms lead time) before each firing cycle.
- [ ] **AC5 — Explode button:** A button on-screen destroys a random Phaser enemy with an explosion animation when clicked.
- [ ] **AC6 — Toggle shoot button:** A button toggles whether Phasers fire. When off, Phasers only orbit. When on, they fire in predictable repeating cycles.
- [ ] **AC7 — Enemy pass-through verified:** Phasers pass freely through each other without collision (per GDD §2.6).
- [ ] **AC8 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript.
- **Gym scope:** This scene is a standalone gym scene (not shipped with the game) — no player ship, no other enemy types, no HUD, no power-ups.
- **Enemy behaviour:** Phasers are 1 HP, destroyed by a single bullet. No health bar needed.
- **Orbital paths:** Multiple Phasers can have different orbital radii or phases to create visual interest without collision.
- **Firing:** When shoot mode is toggled on, Phasers fire in predictable, repeating cycles. Patterns should be learnable and memorizable.
- **Audio:** Play distinct sound effects for spawn, orbital hum, advance audio cue (≥ 500 ms before fire), and destruction.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPhaser.ts` — The Phaser gym scene.
- `src/entities/Phaser.ts` — Phaser enemy entity (orbital movement + pattern firing logic).
- `src/assets/` — Phaser sprite (magenta circular ring with core).
- `src/audio/` — Phaser-related sound effects (spawn, orbital hum, advance cue, destruction).

## Related work

- **Create E1 Scout gym scene (AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q)** — related; implements V-formation pattern.
- **Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes (AH-0MT985FOA008JWM9)** — related; will refactor code across enemy gym scenes.
- **Gym index scene (AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ)** — related; will link to this scene from the gym index.
- **Game Design Document (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5)** — authoritative spec, §4.1 E4 Phaser definition.

## Best practices (mandatory — see docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md)

This scene MUST be built on the shared core gym formation-scene library and follow the conventions documented in **`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`** (see §3 "Best practice: adding a new enemy gym scene" and §5 "Extending the core library"). In particular:

- Extend `GymFormationScene` (src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts) wherever the scene is a formation-driven gym scene; supply only entity-specific configuration (`EnemyFormationConfig`), constants, and thin test accessors — DO NOT copy the ~200-line formation/UI/bullet boilerplate from the pre-refactor `GymScout`/`GymDiver`/`GymTank`.
- Movement that exceeds `applyFormationPosition()`'s flat-translation contract (e.g. E4 orbital paths, E5 clusters, Boss phases) belongs in the **entity** or as a new seam in the core library per §5 — never by duplicating scene boilerplate.
- Reuse the shared formation-offset builders in `src/utils/formations.ts` for any grid/formation geometry; add new pure builders there with unit tests.
- Follow the new-scene checklist: `add.existing()` for display-list membership, `lineStyle()` after `clear()` in entity drawing, exported tuning constants, test accessors, and per-scene tests (spawn count, geometry, drift, EXPLODE, SHOOT toggle, `← INDEX`).
- Update `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1/§3 if this scene introduces a new convention.

- [ ] **AC10 — Core library reuse:** The scene extends the shared `GymFormationScene` core library (or an approved core-library seam per §5 of `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`) and contains no duplicated formation/UI/bullet boilerplate.
- [ ] **AC11 — Guide compliance:** The implementation follows the new-scene checklist in `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§3): `add.existing()`, `lineStyle()` after `clear()`, exported constants, test accessors, and per-scene tests.

# Create E5 Swarm gym scene

## Problem statement

Create a Phaser gym scene demonstrating the E5 Swarm enemy — the fast-moving, unpredictable cluster attacker from GDD §4.1. The scene should show its small, diamond-shaped neon entities moving in tight, fast clusters with sudden direction changes. This is the highest-threat regular enemy by positional threat in dense formations.

## Users

- **Player / developer** testing enemy behaviour — wants to see the Swarm's fast, chaotic cluster movement in isolation.
- **AI agents implementing AI_Hell** — need a reference implementation of swarm/clustering movement patterns.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want to see Swarm enemies move in tight, fast-moving clusters that change direction suddenly so I can verify the cluster movement logic.
- As a **developer**, I want to click a button to destroy a random Swarm enemy and see its explosion animation so I can verify destruction logic.
- As a **developer**, I want to toggle the Swarm's shooting behaviour on/off so I can test both cluster-only and shooting modes independently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Gym scene exists:** A Phaser scene (`src/scenes/gym/GymSwarm.ts`) renders Swarm enemies in tight, fast-moving clusters.
- [ ] **AC2 — Swarm visual style:** Swarms render as small, diamond-shaped neon entities (blue `#0066ff` per GDD §4.1) in groups, consistent with the player ship aesthetic.
- [ ] **AC3 — Cluster movement:** Enemies move in tight, fast-moving clusters that change direction suddenly. Clusters stay together but can split and rejoin.
- [ ] **AC4 — Explode button:** A button on-screen destroys a random Swarm enemy with an explosion animation when clicked.
- [ ] **AC5 — Toggle shoot button:** A button toggles whether Swarms fire coordinated burst shots (simulating Level 4 behaviour). When off, Swarms only cluster. When on, they fire coordinated bursts.
- [ ] **AC6 — Enemy pass-through verified:** Swarms pass freely through each other without collision (per GDD §2.6).
- [ ] **AC7 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

- **Gym scope:** This scene is a standalone gym scene (not shipped with the game) — no player ship, no other enemy types, no HUD, no power-ups.
- **Enemy behaviour:** Swarms are 1 HP, destroyed by a single bullet. No health bar needed.
- **Cluster dynamics:** Swarms should feel fast and unpredictable. Clusters of 3–5 enemies move together, can split and rejoin.
- **Firing:** When shoot mode is toggled on, Swarms fire coordinated bursts (multiple enemies firing simultaneously in the same direction).
- **Audio:** Play distinct sound effects for spawn, fast movement whoosh, and destruction (sharp, quick sound).

- `src/entities/Swarm.ts` — Swarm enemy entity (cluster movement + coordinated firing logic).

# Create Boss (Central AI) gym scene

## Problem statement

Create a Phaser gym scene demonstrating the Boss — "The Central AI" from GDD §4.3. The scene should show its multi-phase health bar, 3–4 distinct attack pattern phases, and complex bullet patterns. This is the final challenge enemy with unique mechanics (multi-hit health, phase transitions).

## Users

- **Player / developer** testing boss behaviour — wants to see all boss attack phases, health bar, and bullet patterns in isolation.
- **AI agents implementing AI_Hell** — need a reference implementation of multi-phase boss behaviour with health bar management.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want to see the Boss cycle through 3–4 distinct attack pattern phases so I can verify the phase transition logic.
- As a **developer**, I want to see a 4-phase health bar that visually depletes as the Boss takes damage so I can verify the health bar rendering.
- As a **developer**, I want to click a button to deal damage to the Boss so I can test health bar progression and phase transitions.
- As a **developer**, I want to see clear visual and audio cues before each boss attack phase begins so I can verify the telegraphing system.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Gym scene exists:** A Phaser scene (`src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts`) renders the Boss enemy with all attack patterns.
- [ ] **AC2 — Boss visual style:** The Central AI renders as a large, imposing neon entity with a visible central core, consistent with a "boss" aesthetic.
- [ ] **AC3 — Multi-phase health bar:** A 4-phase health bar is displayed; each phase depletes independently. The Boss cycles through 3–4 distinct attack patterns as health phases progress.
- [ ] **AC4 — Boss attack phases implemented:** All Boss phases from the GDD are present:
  - **Phase 1:** Spread — Boss fires bullets in a wide spread pattern.
  - **Phase 2:** Spiral — Bullets spiral outward from the Boss in a rotating pattern.
  - **Phase 3:** Pulse — Screen-wide pulse wave expands from the Boss, followed by aimed shots at the player's last known position.
  - **Phase 4 — Desperation:** All previous patterns combined at higher speed; Boss core becomes more exposed/bright (visual cue).
- [ ] **AC5 — Damage button:** A button on-screen deals damage to the Boss, advancing the health bar through phases. Visual cues (core exposure) change at each phase transition.
- [ ] **AC6 — Telegraphing:** Each attack phase begins with clear tell animations and advance audio cues (≥ 500 ms lead time) before the visual event.
- [ ] **AC7 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript.
- **Gym scope:** This scene is a standalone gym scene (not shipped with the game) — no player ship, no other enemy types, no HUD beyond health bar, no power-ups.
- **Enemy behaviour:** The Boss is multi-hit (4 phases). Each phase has a distinct visual representation and attack pattern.
- **Phase transitions:** Visual cues (core exposure, brightness) indicate phase progression. Audio cues announce transitions.
- **Firing:** All Boss attack phases fire complex bullet patterns. Patterns should be learnable but increasingly difficult as phases progress.
- **Audio:** Play distinct sound effects for spawn, each phase's unique audio cue, phase transitions, and destruction.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — The Boss gym scene.
- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — Boss enemy entity (multi-phase health + attack patterns).
- `src/assets/` — Boss sprite (large, imposing neon entity with core).
- `src/audio/` — Boss-related sound effects (spawn, phase cues, transitions, destruction).

## Related work

- **Create E1 Scout gym scene (AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q)** — related; implements V-formation pattern.
- **Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes (AH-0MT985FOA008JWM9)** — related; will refactor code across enemy gym scenes.
- **Gym index scene (AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ)** — related; will link to this scene from the gym index.
- **Game Design Document (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5)** — authoritative spec, §4.3 Boss Design (The Central AI).

## Best practices (mandatory — see docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md)

This scene MUST be built on the shared core gym formation-scene library and follow the conventions documented in **`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`** (see §3 "Best practice: adding a new enemy gym scene" and §5 "Extending the core library"). In particular:

- Extend `GymFormationScene` (src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts) wherever the scene is a formation-driven gym scene; supply only entity-specific configuration (`EnemyFormationConfig`), constants, and thin test accessors — DO NOT copy the ~200-line formation/UI/bullet boilerplate from the pre-refactor `GymScout`/`GymDiver`/`GymTank`.
- Movement that exceeds `applyFormationPosition()`'s flat-translation contract (e.g. E4 orbital paths, E5 clusters, Boss phases) belongs in the **entity** or as a new seam in the core library per §5 — never by duplicating scene boilerplate.
- Reuse the shared formation-offset builders in `src/utils/formations.ts` for any grid/formation geometry; add new pure builders there with unit tests.
- Follow the new-scene checklist: `add.existing()` for display-list membership, `lineStyle()` after `clear()` in entity drawing, exported tuning constants, test accessors, and per-scene tests (spawn count, geometry, drift, EXPLODE, SHOOT toggle, `← INDEX`).
- Update `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1/§3 if this scene introduces a new convention.

- [ ] **AC9 — Core library reuse:** The scene extends the shared `GymFormationScene` core library or its documented extension seam (§5 of `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`) where applicable (Boss phase/health extensions may compose with the base class) and contains no duplicated formation/UI/bullet boilerplate.
- [ ] **AC10 — Guide compliance:** The implementation follows `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §3–§5: `add.existing()`, `lineStyle()` after `clear()`, exported constants, test accessors, and per-scene tests.

Define ShipConfig type, defaults, load, and save functions

## Goal

Create the ship configuration module that serves as the single source of truth for ship tuning values.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — ShipConfig interface:** A typed interface exports all configurable ship values:
  - thrustAcceleration: number (default 600)
  - maxSpeed: number (default 350)
  - shipSize: number (default 20)
  - thrustFlameLength: number (default 0.75)
  - shipColor: number (default 0x00ffff)
  - thrustFlameColor: number (default 0xff8c00)
  - thrustFlameInnerColor: number (default 0xffff00)

- [ ] **AC2 — Default config:** A DEFAULT_CONFIG: ShipConfig object holds the current hard-coded values.

- [ ] **AC3 — loadShipConfig():** Returns ShipConfig by reading localStorage (key: ai-hell-ship-config) and parsing JSON. If the key does not exist or parsing fails, returns DEFAULT_CONFIG.

- [ ] **AC4 — saveShipConfig(values: ShipConfig):** Serializes values as JSON and writes to localStorage under key ai-hell-ship-config.

- [ ] **AC5 — Module location:** New file at src/core/config.ts. Exports: ShipConfig, DEFAULT_CONFIG, loadShipConfig, saveShipConfig.

## Key Files

- src/core/constants.ts — current source of hard-coded values; will be updated to re-export from config.
- src/utils/movement.ts — consumes thrust/maxSpeed via MovementConfig.
- src/entities/Player.ts — consumes SHIP_SIZE, colours, THRUST_ACCELERATION, MAX_SPEED.

## Goal

Wire the new config module into the existing code so ship tuning values flow from the config file (localStorage) instead of only hard-coded constants.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — constants.ts re-exports:** src/core/constants.ts re-exports DEFAULT_CONFIG values so existing imports (THRUST_ACCELERATION, MAX_SPEED, SHIP_SIZE, THRUST_FLAME_LENGTH, SHIP_COLOR, THRUST_FLAME_COLOR, THRUST_FLAME_INNER_COLOR) still resolve with defaults unchanged.
- [ ] **AC2 — Player consumes runtime config:** src/entities/Player.ts reads the config (via loadShipConfig or injected values) and uses it for MovementConfig (thrust, maxSpeed), shipSize rendering, and flame rendering, instead of importing constants directly.
- [ ] **AC3 — Config values can be updated at runtime:** Player exposes a way to update its config (e.g. setConfig) so a future gym slider can live-tune values; when called, the ship re-renders and physics config updates.

## Problem statement

The player ship's thrust flame keeps its current animated length when the pressed direction keys change (e.g. switching from Up to Left, or adding/removing a direction key mid-thrust). The flame simply re-orients to the new direction while keeping its length (see the 'flame's direction changed while a flame is visible' redraw branch in src/entities/Player.ts::preUpdate). The producer wants each change of the pressed keys to start a fresh flame burst from length 0.

## Desired change

When the set of pressed direction keys (up/down/left/right) changes while the ship is still thrusting, the animated flame length must reset to 0 (fresh burst) and regrow from there in the new direction, at the normal growth rate (proportional to thrustAcceleration).

- Pressed-key change while a direction is held → the flame restarts from length 0 on that frame; regrowth begins immediately at the existing rate.
- Releasing ALL keys keeps the existing decay semantics (decay at 4× growth rate; length never below 0) — no stuck flame on release. The reset applies to direction changes (still thrusting), not to full release.
- Unchanged held keys must NOT reset the flame (normal growth/decay continue).
- Existing feel tuning (FLAME_GROWTH_TIME_AT_REF = 0.03 s), framerate independence (delta-time based), and config-live max length are unchanged.

discovered-from:AH-0MTAF5YLT009TXAM

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Changing the pressed keys while thrusting resets the observable flame length (getFlameLength()) to 0 on that frame (a zero-delta change frame shows exactly 0; with real dt the flame regrows from 0).
- AC2: The flame regrows from 0 in the new direction at the normal growth rate (higher thrustAcceleration → reaches full faster).
- AC3: Releasing all keys still decays the flame at 4× the growth rate to 0 — no stuck flame on release (decay path unchanged; release does not force an instant reset).
- AC4: Holding the same keys does not reset the length — the flame continues growing/decaying normally frame to frame.
- AC5: Full test suite and tsc build remain green; docs (Player.ts header, GDD §2.2) updated to describe the reset-on-direction-change behavior.
data.title: Reset thrust flame length to 0 when the pressed keys change

# Create gym scene for non-combat power-ups (P5 Speed Boost, P8 Extra Life, P9 Magnet) with round-robin spawning, collection, and standalone power-up HUD

## Problem statement

The gym suite (GymIndex + per-mechanic scenes) currently has no scene demonstrating power-up spawning, collection, and HUD feedback: the existing gym scenes explicitly exclude HUD and power-ups. This item adds a single `GymPowerUps` scene (auto-discovered by the gym index) that cycles through the **non-weapon, non-combat** power-ups **P5 Speed Boost, P8 Extra Life, P9 Magnet** round-robin — each spawns every 5 s, grows from nothing to full size, sits stationary for 5 s, shrinks to nothing and despawns — while the player ship flies around collecting them. Collected power-ups apply their **full behaviour** (observable without threats) and their states (timers, stack counts, lives) are rendered by a **standalone HUD class** designed to be attachable to any Phaser scene.

> **Scope boundary (per operator, three-way split):**
> - **Weapon power-ups** (P1 Spread Shot, P2 Rapid Fire + new weapon patterns) → sibling **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** ("Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene", in-progress).
> - **Combat-coupled power-ups** (P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, P7 Teleport — full behaviour demonstrable only with threats) → sibling **AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40** ("Create combat gym scene for combat-coupled power-ups… with low-level enemy threats").
> - **This item = non-combat, threat-free gym: P5, P8, P9**, plus the shared spawn/lifecycle mechanics, ship, and the standalone HUD class (the combat scene depends on this item for those reusable pieces).

## Users

- **Player / developer testing the game** — wants to see each non-combat power-up spawn, grow, sit, shrink, and fade in isolation, and to verify collection + effect application + HUD feedback feel right before any combat is added.
- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — need a reusable power-up lifecycle (spawn/grow/hold/shrink/collect), per-type effect behaviour, and a standalone HUD that any future scene (main game, other gyms, the combat gym) can attach.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want to fly over a grown power-up to collect it, so I can see its effect take hold (e.g., a faster ship, a lives bump, drops drifting toward me) and watch it appear on the HUD.
- As a **player**, I want the HUD to show the active power-ups with remaining timers (timed types) and counts (stackable/permanent types), so I always know what is currently active.
- As a **developer**, I want re-collecting a timed power-up to refresh its timer to the full duration, so repeated pickups behave predictably.
- As a **developer**, I want the HUD to be a standalone class any scene can instantiate, so the main game and the combat gym don't have to re-implement power-up status UI.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Single gym scene with ship:** A new `GymPowerUps` scene (key `GymPowerUps`, label `PowerUps`) is defined in `src/scenes/gym/`, auto-discovered and listed by the gym index, boots correctly, renders the player ship with the standard thrust movement + screen-wrap from `GymPlayer`, and has the shared "← INDEX" back button.
- [ ] **AC2 — Round-robin spawn/lifecycle:** The scene spawns exactly the non-combat power-ups **P5, P8, P9 in ascending GDD order (P5 Speed Boost, P8 Extra Life, P9 Magnet)**, one every 5 s, each remaining stationary for a 5 s lifetime. On spawn the drop **grows from scale 0 to full size**; on despawn it **shrinks to nothing** then is removed; growth/shrink are delta-time driven (framerate-independent) and the window durations are tunable constants.
- [ ] **AC3 — Collection rule:** A drop is collectible only while its current scale is **> 3% of full size** (i.e., during grow, full-size hold, and shrink until it drops below the threshold); collecting requires the ship to overlap the drop. A drop that fades uncollected is removed with no effect.
- [ ] **AC4 — Full per-type behaviour (threat-free):** Collecting each type applies its full GDD §4.4 behaviour as observable without threats: **P5 Speed Boost** — +50% movement speed (thrust/max-speed) applied live to the ship's movement for 10 s; **P8 Extra Life** — +1 life immediately (cap 5, excess ignored), reflected in the HUD lives counter (starting at 3); **P9 Magnet** — permanent effect, one stack per pickup (cap 5), radius 2× ship size +50% per stack, attracting on-screen power-up drops toward the ship at a speed slower than the ship's max speed.
- [ ] **AC5 — Timer refresh:** Re-collecting an already-active timed power-up (P5) refreshes its timer to the full duration (not additive, not ignored). Permanent/passive types follow their own rules (P9 stacks to cap 5 then no-op; P8 excess ignored above cap 5).
- [ ] **AC6 — Standalone HUD class:** A standalone `src/ui/HUD.ts` class (Phaser game-object based, attachable to any scene, rendered above gameplay) shows, for each active power-up: **icon, name, and either a remaining-seconds timer (timed types) or a stack/pickup count (P9 magnet stacks)**, plus the **lives count** (P8). The gym scene uses this HUD; the class contains no gym-specific logic and is reusable by the combat gym scene (AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40).

# Create combat gym scene for combat-coupled power-ups (P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, P7 Teleport) with low-level enemy threats

## Problem statement

Four power-up types in the GDD catalogue — **P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, P7 Teleport** — cannot demonstrate their full behaviour without threats: Shield must absorb a hit, Bomb must clear on-screen enemy bullets, Phase Shift must pass through enemies and bullets, and Teleport must search for a safe spot free of threats. The operator split these "combat-coupled" types out of the threat-free power-up gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) into this dedicated **combat gym scene** that contains a **low-level enemy threat (E1 Scout with shooting)**. The scene shares the round-robin spawn lifecycle, grow-shrink animation, 3% collection threshold, player ship, and standalone HUD class with the non-combat gym, on which this item depends.

## Users

- **Player / developer testing the game** — wants to see each combat-coupled power-up's full effect against real (but low-level) threats: a shield bubble popping on a hit, a bomb wiping a bullet cloud, ghosting straight through a formation, and blinking away to a safe spot.
- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — need the threat-coupled behaviour (hit absorption, bullet clearing, intangibility, safe-spot resolution) implemented and tested once, in a form the main game can reuse.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want my shield bubble to absorb exactly one hit and pop, so I can verify the GDD's "absorbs one hit" rule.
- As a **player**, I want to collect a Bomb while scouts are firing and see every on-screen enemy bullet vanish, with enemies untouched (they are 1 HP, GDD §4.4).
- As a **player**, I want Phase Shift to let me fly straight through the scout formation and its bullets without being hit, for 3 seconds.
- As a **player**, I want to press Space with a collected Teleport to jump to the nearest safe spot (free of scouts and bullets) along my travel direction, gaining Phase Shift on arrival.
- As a **developer**, I want the ship's hit response (no shield/phase shift) to be a simple flash/reset with no lives counter, so the demo keeps a pure combat focus.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Combat scene with ship + low-level threats:** A new `GymPowerUpsCombat` scene (key `GymPowerUpsCombat`, label `PowerUps Combat`) is defined in `src/scenes/gym/`, auto-discovered and listed by the gym index, boots correctly, renders the player ship with standard thrust movement + screen-wrap, and contains a **formation of E1 Scout enemies** (reusing `src/entities/Scout.ts` + the formation utilities) with a **SHOOT toggle** that enables aimed enemy fire at the **ship's live position** (not the fixed demo target), so hits are demonstrable. Shared "← INDEX" back button present.
- [ ] **AC2 — Round-robin spawn/lifecycle:** The scene spawns exactly the combat-coupled power-ups **P3, P4, P6, P7 in ascending GDD order**, one every 5 s, each remaining stationary for a 5 s lifetime; spawn = **grow from scale 0 to full size**, despawn = **shrink to nothing**; growth/shrink delta-time driven with the same tunable constants as the non-combat gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT).
- [ ] **AC3 — Collection rule:** A drop is collectible only while its current scale is **> 3% of full size** (grow, hold, and shrink until below threshold); collection requires the ship to overlap the drop; an uncollected drop fades with no effect.
- [ ] **AC4 — P3 Shield full behaviour:** Collecting P3 arms a shield bubble rendered around the ship for **15 s**; the bubble **absorbs exactly one hit** (enemy body or enemy bullet) and then pops (effect ends, no ship flash/reset for that hit); if never hit, it expires after 15 s. Re-collection while active refreshes the timer to 15 s.
- [ ] **AC5 — P4 Bomb full behaviour:** Collecting P4 instantly removes **all on-screen enemy bullets** (aimed scout fire in-flight), does **not damage enemies** (GDD §4.4 note), is not a timed effect, and shows a brief HUD notice. Re-collection while enemies are not firing is a benign no-op (bullets cleared anyway).
- [ ] **AC6 — P6 Phase Shift full behaviour:** Collecting P6 renders a ghost-outline ship for **3 s** during which the ship **passes through enemy bodies and enemy bullets without being hit**; hit checks are disabled for the duration. Re-collection refreshes the timer to 3 s.
- [ ] **AC7 — P7 Teleport full behaviour:** P7 **stacks FIFO** (each pickup = one use); pressing **Space** consumes the earliest-collected use and teleports the ship **along the current travel direction to the nearest safe spot** — a position free of enemy bodies and enemy bullets in a safety radius, clamped to screen bounds; if no safe spot exists in the travel direction, the ship teleports to the nearest on-screen safe position anyway; on arrival the ship **gains P6 Phase Shift (3 s)** per GDD. HUD shows the teleport count.
- [ ] **AC8 — Hit response (no shield/phase shift):** Being hit by an enemy body or enemy bullet with no active P3/P6 triggers a **simple flash/reset with no lives counter** (e.g., brief invulnerability + reposition), per operator decision; this is the only consequence — no lives, no game over.
- [ ] **AC9 — HUD reuse:** The scene uses the **standalone HUD class from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** (`src/ui/HUD.ts`) unchanged for active-effect icons, names, timers (P3/P6), and counts (P7); **no lives counter** in this scene; the HUD class itself is not modified with gym/combat-specific logic (any extension lives in the scene).
- [ ] **AC10 — Testing/validation:** Unit tests cover: P3 absorb-then-pop on a hit + 15 s expiry + refresh; P4 clearing all bullets without enemy damage; P6 pass-through (no hits during 3 s) + refresh; P7 FIFO stack/consume, safe-spot resolution (avoiding scouts/bullets, clamped), fallback when no safe spot, and P6-on-arrival; hit-response flash/reset (no lives); round-robin order. Scene-level tests (gameHarness) verify discovery, ship presence, scout formation + SHOOT toggle, collection against live bullets, and back button. Full suite green.
- [ ] **AC11 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (GDD §6.4 architecture gains `GymPowerUpsCombat`).
- [ ] **AC12 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine/stack:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript, Vite, Vitest (locked). Neon-vector aesthetic; code-drawn graphics only — **no external art assets**; icons code-drawn per GDD §4.4 suggestions.
- **Threats:** **E1 Scout only** (operator decision) — reuse `src/entities/Scout.ts` as-is; formation via existing utilities; **shooting toggle** enabled for the demo (bullets aimed at the ship's live position). No E2/E3/E4/E5/Boss.
- **No lives model:** hit response is flash/reset only (operator decision); P8 lives is out of scope (it lives in the non-combat gym).
- **Weapon power-ups out of scope:** P1/P2/new weapon patterns belong to AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR; the ship's auto-fire is NOT part of this scene (Bomb does not damage enemies, so no fire needed).
- **Shared mechanics:** the spawn cadence (one per 5 s, 5 s lifetime, 0.5 s grow/shrink) and the 3% collection threshold match the non-combat gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT); constants stay in `src/core/constants.ts`; the HUD class is reused unchanged (dependency on that item).
- **Hit model details:** overlap = ship hull radius + enemy/bullet radius, exactly as the GDD "enemies are the bullets" §2.4 model; shield/phase-shift suppress the hit response; teleport safe radius is a tunable constant (proposal: ~3× ship size).

## Existing state

- Non-combat power-up gym **AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** (intake_complete, open) delivers, first: `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` (base lifecycle), the type catalogue + icons, `src/ui/HUD.ts` (standalone), the spawn/lifecycle constants, and `GymPowerUps` — **this item depends on those reusable pieces**. This item adds the P3/P4/P6/P7 catalogue entries + threat-coupled effect hooks.
- `src/entities/Scout.ts` exists with `tryFireAimedBullet` (currently aimed at a fixed demo target), formation offsets, alive/destroy lifecycle; `GymScout` demonstrates a V-formation with EXPLODE/SHOOT buttons via the shared `GymFormationScene` core library (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`).
- Ship + thrust movement exist (`src/entities/Player.ts`, `src/utils/movement.ts`, `GymPlayer.ts`).
- GDD §4.4 defines P3/P4/P6/P7 semantics and icon suggestions; §4.4 notes Bomb does not damage 1-HP enemies; §2.3 lives model (out of scope here, replaced by flash/reset).
- Tests use Vitest + a gameHarness (`src/test/gameHarness.ts`) with happy-dom.

## Desired change

1. Extend the power-up catalogue from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT with **P3/P4/P6/P7** entries (id, name, icon, duration/stack semantics, threat-coupled effect hooks), following the same `src/powerups/` layout.
2. Add `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — ship (reused `Player` + movement), a Scout V-formation with a SHOOT toggle (bullets aimed at the ship), the shared round-robin spawner (P3 → P4 → P6 → P7), grow/hold/shrink lifecycle, 3% collection gate, threat-coupled effect application (shield absorb, bomb clear, phase shift pass-through, teleport safe-spot), flash/reset hit response, HUD attachment (reused), back button.
3. Ship-aimed fire: extend or parameterise the Scout's fire target so bullets aim at the ship's live position (implementation may pass the ship position into the scene's fire-collection path).
4. Add safe-spot resolution (enemy/bullet-aware) + teleport consumption to `src/powerups/effects.ts`; add hit-check suppression for shield/phase-shift in the scene collision pass.
5. Update the GDD §6.4 architecture briefly (list `GymPowerUpsCombat`; note threat-coupled effects as implemented).
6. Tests: unit tests for P3/P4/P6/P7 behaviours + scene tests via gameHarness.

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — **new** combat gym scene (the deliverable).
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — extend the catalogue from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT with **P3/P4/P6/P7** entries.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — extend with shield-absorb state, bomb bullet-clear, phase-shift hit suppression, teleport safe-spot resolution + FIFO consumption.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — extend with P3/P4/P6/P7 code-drawn icons.
- `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` — **reused** (depends on AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — **reused unchanged** (depends on AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT).
- `src/entities/Scout.ts` — possibly parameterised aim target (ship position) for `tryFireAimedBullet`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts` (+ P3/P4/P6/P7 unit tests) — **new** tests.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — teleport safe radius + travelled distance, hit-reset values (extend the shared constants).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §6.4 architecture: add `GymPowerUpsCombat`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** — "Create gym scene for power-ups with spawning, collection, and standalone HUD" (the non-combat gym): **prerequisite** — supplies the shared PowerUp lifecycle, catalogue, icons, HUD class, and spawn/lifecycle constants this item reuses/extends. Dependency edge: this item → AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT.
- **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** — "Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene" (in-progress): sibling — weapon power-ups excluded here, same round-robin/grow-shrink/3% mechanics.
- **"Create E1 Scout gym scene" / GymScout** — precedent for the Scout formation, EXPLODE/SHOOT buttons, and the `GymFormationScene` core-library pattern (AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q completed; core-library refactor AH-0MT987VA3005YBNK / AH-0MTAN4IFR007U9B3 completed).
- **"Create gym scene with player ship and thrust-based space movement" (AH-0MT97OA3E001DOYW)** — precedent for `Player` reuse.
- GDD power-up catalog items (completed): "Redesign P7 Dash…" (AH-0MT7UY5UR002LD5U), "Add a Magnet power up" (AH-0MT7VE4SX0005A8V), "Add an extra life power up" (AH-0MT7UX8LE0072MR3) — semantics source for P7/P9/P8 (P3/P4/P6 remain as defined in GDD §4.4).
- GDD items (completed): "Game Design Document for AI_Hell" (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Dependency:** this item assumes the non-combat gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) lands first (PowerUp lifecycle, catalogue, HUD, constants). If that item is delayed, the combat scene work is blocked — do not build parallel copies of the lifecycle/HUD.
- **Assumption — ship-aimed fire:** Scout's `tryFireAimedBullet` currently aims at a fixed demo target; the combat scene requires bullets aimed at the ship's live position. Implement by parameterising the aim target (small, contained change) rather than duplicating the Scout entity.
- **Assumption — teleport safe spot:** "nearest safe spot in the travel direction" = first empty position along the travel ray where no enemy body or bullet occupies a safety-radius disc (tunable, proposal 3× ship size), clamped to screen bounds; fallback = nearest on-screen safe position (GDD); P6 granted on arrival.
- **Assumption — hit response flash/reset:** a hit without shield/phase shift flashes the ship and repositions it (or grants brief invulnerability) — exact demo values tunable; no lives, no game over (operator Q8).
